notes_list.title: Factors of a Number
notes_list.basic_overview: If N = p^a x q^b x r^c: total factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1); prime factors (with repetition) = a+b+c; distinct prime factors = number of different primes.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Odd factors: ignore the prime 2 and apply the formula to the rest. Even factors = total - odd. Example 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5: total 16, prime factors 5, distinct primes 3, odd factors 4, even factors 12.

notes_list.title: Multiples of 6 but not of 18
notes_list.basic_overview: Count multiples of 6, subtract multiples of 18 (their LCM-based overlap), using integer division.

notes_list.title: Euler / Fermat Remainder Trick
notes_list.basic_overview: If a and n are co-prime, a^phi(n) leaves remainder 1 when divided by n. For a prime n, phi(n) = n - 1.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Example: 2^102 divided by 101: phi(101) = 100, so 2^102 = 2^2 = 4 remainder 4. Example: 3^21 divided by 5: phi(5) = 4, 21 = 4x5 + 1, so remainder 3.

notes_list.title: Division by 98 and 99
notes_list.basic_overview: By 98: count the hundreds, add 2 for each hundred to the leftover, then adjust. 2352 / 98: 23 hundreds, 23 x 2 = 46, 46 + 52 = 98 = one more, so quotient 24.
notes_list.extra_info_content: By 99: split the number into 2-digit blocks from the right. 2345 / 99: blocks 23 and 45; quotient = 23, remainder = 23 + 45 = 68. This works when the block sum is less than 99. For 49 (round up to 50, base 5): 3234 / 49: 323 / 5 is about 6; 6 x 49 = 294; 323 - 294 = 29; bring down 4 and divide 294 by 49 = 6 exactly. Answer: 66.

notes_list.title: Sum of Squares
notes_list.extra_info_content: Example n = 10: 10 x 11 x 21 / 6 = 385. The 6 in the denominator always cancels with factors 2 and 3 from the numerator.

notes_list.title: Squares Near 50 and 100
notes_list.extra_info_content: Near 50: N^2 = (25 +/- d) | d^2, d^2 as 2 digits. 53^2 = (25+3) | 09 = 2809. A number ending in 5 always has a square ending in 25.

notes_list.title: Square Root of (a + 2 sqrt(b))
notes_list.basic_overview: Rewrite the surd in the form 2 sqrt(m), then find two numbers whose product is m and whose sum is a.
notes_list.extra_info_content: sqrt(7 + sqrt48) = sqrt(7 + 2 sqrt12); find two numbers with product 12 and sum 7: 4 and 3, so the answer is sqrt4 + sqrt3 = 2 + sqrt3.

notes_list.title: Adding Mixed Fractions (same denominator)
notes_list.basic_overview: Add whole parts and numerators separately: (whole1 + whole2) x denominator + (num1 + num2), all over the denominator.
notes_list.extra_info_content: 6 3/8 + 5 4/8 = (11 x 8 + 7) / 8 = 95/8. Works only when denominators are equal.

notes_list.title: Algebra Identity in Calculation Questions
notes_list.basic_overview: a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2). If the denominator already equals the second bracket, the answer is simply (a - b).

notes_list.title: Inradius of a Right-Angled Triangle
notes_list.basic_overview: r = (P + B - H) / 2, where P and B are the perpendicular sides and H is the hypotenuse. Area of the incircle = pi r^2.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Example: sides 12, 16, 20: r = (12 + 16 - 20)/2 = 4 cm; area = pi x 16 = about 50.27 sq cm.
